correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed all three disjoint cases. A subdivision w_ij has N[w_ij]={a_i,b_j,w_ij}, so omitted original vertices cannot occupy both sides. If no originals are omitted, selected subdivision edges must cover all originals, giving E_{p,q}. Omitting u>=1 from A forces exactly uq subdivisions, with remaining p-u selected rows independently nonempty; this gives C(p,u)z^(p+q+u(q-1))U_q^(p-u), and the omitted-B term is symmetric. Minimum exponents in these classes are 2p+q+u(q-2) and p+2q+v(p-2); the p=2 and p=q=2 boundary multiplicities are counted without double-counting. New independent closed-neighborhood bitmap enumeration directly tested all 2^(p+q+pq) subsets for (2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3): 51,456 candidate subsets, matching every polynomial coefficient and minimum multiplicities 12,31,87,6. The three-case bijection, not finite tests, proves the all-p,q theorem.

final_claim: For 2<=p<=q, the at-least-two closed-neighborhood domination polynomial of S(K_{p,q}) equals z^(p+q)[E_{p,q}+(U_q+z^(q-1))^p-U_q^p+(U_p+z^(p-1))^q-U_p^q], with U_r=(1+z)^r-1. Minimum size p+2q has multiplicity 12 at (2,2), 3^q+2q-2 for p=2<q, and the surjection count Sum_{j=0}^p(-1)^j*C(p,j)*(p-j)^q when p>=3.
